Question: How do you see the recent round of layoffs in start-ups in India?
Answer: According to data shared by data analytics firm Tracxn Technologies with Moneycontrol, only 23 of the 100 unicorns, or startups valued at $1 billion or more, have managed to achieve profitability for a financial year. Investors pour their money into these startups for profit. When there is no profit there would be cost-cutting, which would result in layoffs. You may have the best ideas and technologies in the world, but it would be of no value unless you generate a profit out of it(unless it is an NGO). So these layoffs don’t really surprise me. And it’s not just startups in India, the picture remains the same all over the world. Coinbase, one of the world’s biggest startups also hit hard. Graph showing global startup employees laid off per month. April-June 2022 had been the worst month since the pandemic. Also, central banks all over the world have begun raising interest rates, making it more expensive to borrow money to fund the aggressive expansion of money-losing tech companies in the hope that they’ll one day turn a profit. All these factors alongside, the Ukraine-Russia war, global chip shortage, supply chain issue, and post-pandemic normalcy have also been contributing factors to these recent layoffs in startups. Question: Does everyone in the corporate world call each other by their first names? Even if they are senior to you?
